skill.name: esimaccess-api
skill.description: Manage eSIM Access API workflows for package discovery, HMAC-signed requests, orders, ICCID lookup, data usage, top-ups, profile actions, webhooks, refunds, and reissues.
skill.summary: Guides authenticated eSIM Access API operations across ordering, lifecycle management, usage, and webhooks.
skill.author: esimaccess

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, JavaScript template literals, and documented API URLs. No prompt injection evidence was found. The main risks are semantic: the bundled test script can perform live production account changes and can print sensitive eSIM provisioning data.

remediation.issue: The test script performs paid and state-changing production API operations.
remediation.suggestion: Default the script to read-only or dry-run mode. Require explicit flags for order creation, SMS, suspend, unsuspend, cancel, and refund tests.

remediation.issue: The test script prints sensitive account and eSIM provisioning data.
remediation.suggestion: Mask access codes, ICCIDs, IMSIs, EIDs, order numbers, QR code URLs, and short URLs by default. Add a verbose mode for local debugging.

remediation.issue: The testing instructions do not warn users about production side effects.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear warning before the test command that it uses live endpoints and can spend balance or modify eSIM profiles.

semantic_findings.title: Live Test Script Can Mutate Paid eSIM Accounts
semantic_findings.description: The bundled test script can create an order when balance is sufficient, then suspend, unsuspend, send SMS, and cancel against the user account. The testing command in SKILL.md does not warn that these are production operations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script directly calls order, suspend, unsuspend, SMS, and cancel endpoints using user credentials. These actions can spend balance or alter active eSIM state.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive eSIM Data Printed to Console
semantic_findings.description: The script prints an access code prefix, ICCID, eSIM transaction number, order number, IMSI, EID, QR code URL, and short URL. These values can expose subscriber or provisioning data in terminal or CI logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited console output includes direct account and provisioning identifiers. The risk depends on where logs are stored, but the data exposure is explicit.

content.value_statement: eSIM API work requires signed requests, correct identifiers, and careful production actions. This skill guides eSIM Access operations from package lookup through orders, usage, webhooks, and refunds.
actual_capabilities: Explains HMAC-SHA256 signing for Node.js and Python examples.
Guides balance checks, package search, and top-up eligibility lookup.
Supports order creation, status polling, ICCID lookup, and QR provisioning guidance.
Covers usage queries, cancellation, revoke, suspend, unsuspend, SMS, and refund workflows.
Helps configure, query, and interpret webhooks and status or error codes.
Includes a Node.js end-to-end test script for the documented API.
limitations: The skill does not provide eSIM Access credentials or account funding.
Production API calls can spend balance or change eSIM state.
The test script uses live endpoints and is not a sandbox.
API results depend on current account permissions, package availability, and eSIM status.

use_cases.title: Prepare Travel Data Plans
use_cases.description: Find available country packages, compare data volume and duration, and prepare a safe order workflow.

use_cases.title: Support Active eSIMs
use_cases.description: Look up orders, ICCIDs, profile status, data usage, and cancellation eligibility for customer support cases.

use_cases.title: Build API Integrations
use_cases.description: Use the documented HMAC signing flow, endpoint rules, webhook events, and error codes during implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Check Account Balance
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: confirm account funds before any purchase.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me check my eSIM Access account balance. Ask for needed credential details and show the safe request steps.

prompt_templates.title: Find Packages for a Trip
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare plans for a destination.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find eSIM packages for Japan and explain the price, data volume, duration, and top-up support fields.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Refund and Reissue
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: replace an unused eSIM carefully.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a refund and reissue workflow for an unused eSIM. Include status checks, cancellation rules, and confirmation points.

prompt_templates.title: Design Webhook Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an eSIM Access webhook integration. Cover event types, verification, follow-up queries, retries, and operational safeguards.

output_examples.input: I need a 5 GB eSIM for the United States and want to know whether it supports top-ups.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies relevant package fields, explains price conversion, checks supportTopUpType, and recommends confirming cost before ordering.

output_examples.input: My order has an order number but no ICCID yet.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains status polling, expected provisioning delay, webhook fallback, and which fields show readiness for installation.

output_examples.input: I want to cancel an unused eSIM and issue a replacement.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks whether the eSIM is unused, explains refund behavior, confirms the package, and sequences cancellation before replacement.

best_practices: Confirm every purchase, top-up, SMS, suspend, revoke, and cancel action before sending a write request.
Keep accessCode values private and mask eSIM identifiers when sharing logs or support notes.
Use read-only checks before running any live end-to-end test or production workflow.
anti_patterns: Running the full test script against a funded production account without reviewing each operation.
Sharing accessCode values, QR code URLs, ICCIDs, IMSIs, or EIDs in public logs.
Treating cancel and revoke as interchangeable actions without checking activation state and refund rules.

faq.question: Does this skill need my access code?
faq.answer: Yes. API calls require your eSIM Access accessCode. Keep it private and avoid shared terminals or logs.

faq.question: Can it create real orders?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented write operations can create orders, top up plans, send SMS, and change eSIM profile state.

faq.question: Does the test script use a sandbox?
faq.answer: No. The included test script points to live eSIM Access API endpoints.

faq.question: Can it help with top-ups?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains top-up eligibility, the required esimTranNo identifier, and package lookup rules.

faq.question: Can it manage webhooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers webhook save, query, notification types, sender IPs, and follow-up API checks.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
